ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY

NUMBER 2 YEAR 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children have experienced an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic and inseparable manner from one another. Community service is the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY

NUMBER 2 YEAR 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children have experienced an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic and inseparable manner from one another. Community service is the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 26

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:

a. Notification of information on employment opportunities for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.

3. Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

Article 28

2. Implementation of coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall be conducted among stakeholders in a cross-sectoral manner with Regional Apparatus, and community institutions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
3. Implementation of Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b towards women and children who are victims through guidance on religious values and social values, Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance by the Regional Apparatus in charge together with other related Agencies.
4. Implementation of education and training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c shall be provided to women and children who are victims as an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women and children in fulfilling their rights and life needs by the Regional Apparatus in charge, Vocational Training Centers and other related Agencies.
5. Implementation of guidance and supervision towards women and children who are victims as referred to in paragraph (2), paragraph (3) and paragraph (4) shall be conducted through monitoring and evaluation of the targets to be achieved.

Article 15

1. The obligations and responsibilities of the private sector and community as referred to in Article 13 letter b and letter c, shall be implemented in the form of participation of the private sector and community.
2. Forms of participation of the private sector and community as referred to in paragraph (1), include:
a. Preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. Providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. Participating in the handling of victims of violence.
3. Forms of participation of the private sector and community as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY

NUMBER 2 YEAR 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children have experienced an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic and inseparable manner from one another. Community service is the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 26

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

a. Notification of information on employment opportunities for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.

3. Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

Article 10

1. Other violence as referred to in Article 4 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
2. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, with or without the use of means that create fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
3. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY

NUMBER 2 YEAR 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children have experienced an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic and inseparable manner from one another. Community service is the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 28

1. The regional government implements Guidance and Supervision by means of: a. Coordination b. Guidance c. Education and Training d. Monitoring and Evaluation
2. Implementation of coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall be conducted among stakeholders in a cross-sectoral manner with Regional Apparatus, and community institutions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
3. Implementation of Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b towards women and children who are victims through guidance on religious values and social values, Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance by the Regional Apparatus in charge together with other related Agencies.
4. Implementation of education and training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c shall be provided to women and children who are victims as an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women and children in fulfilling their rights and life needs by the Regional Apparatus in charge, Vocational Training Centers and other related Agencies.
5. Implementation of guidance and supervision towards women and children who are victims as referred to in paragraph (2), paragraph (3) and paragraph (4) shall be conducted through monitoring and evaluation of the targets to be achieved.

Article 8

Neglect as referred to in Article 4 letter d includes:
a. Acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood and care to such women.
b. Acts that result in the improper fulfillment of children's needs, whether physical, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care.
c. Acts of deliberately neglecting to care for or look after children as they should be, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care.

Article 9

Exploitation as referred to in Article 4 letter e includes:
a. Acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. Acts with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits.

CHAPTER XII

SANCTIONS

Article 32

In the event of violence against Women and Children, sanctions shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 10

1. Other violence as referred to in Article 4 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
2. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, with or without the use of means that create fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
3. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (1) includes a situation where a person/victim is made to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic and inseparable manner from one another. Community service is the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic and inseparable manner from one another. CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children have experienced an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic and inseparable manner from one another. Community service is the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 33. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 34. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination. 35. Protection of women is all efforts made to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights. 36. Implementation of Child Protection is a series of activities carried out by the Regional Government, community, and parents, aimed at preventing, reducing risks, and handling victims of acts of violence, exploitation, abuse and neglect of children. 37. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, be healthy, intelligent, grow and develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination. 38. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic, social exploitation including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 39. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, and psychologically. 40. Violence Against Women and Children in the Household is any act against a woman and child that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, economically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the household sphere. 41. Exploitation of Children is any act involving children in activities that can harm welfare and growth and development or endanger the safety of children with the aim of enabling others to obtain economic, sexual, social, or political benefits, including if there is a restriction or elimination of opportunities for children to obtain their rights. 42. Child Abuse is any action against a child, including placing the child in a situation that can cause adverse effects on the welfare, safety, dignity and development of the child. 43. Assistance is a social worker who has professional competence in his/her field. 44. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of children who are victims of violence, abuse, exploitation, and or neglect. 48. Care Environment is care by parents and care outside parental care. REGENT OF TANGGAMUS,

a. that in order to protect the constitutional rights of women and children in accordance with the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the Regional Government is obliged to be responsible for the implementation of protection for women and children against acts of violence; b. that to meet the indicators for the Implementation of Child-Friendly Regency, concerning protection services, prevention of violence against women and children, regulations are needed to regulate the various roles of regional apparatus institutions and other institutions; c. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, and letter b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Women and Children; In view of:

Article 26

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:

a. Notification of information on employment opportunities for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.

3. Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 28

1. The regional government implements Guidance and Supervision by means of: a. Coordination b. Guidance c. Education and Training d. Monitoring and Evaluation
2. Implementation of coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall be conducted among stakeholders in a cross-sectoral manner with Regional Apparatus, and community institutions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
3. Implementation of Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b towards women and children who are victims through guidance on religious values and social values, Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance by the Regional Apparatus in charge together with other related Agencies.
4. Implementation of education and training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c shall be provided to women and children who are victims as an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women and children in fulfilling their rights and life needs by the Regional Apparatus in charge, Vocational Training Centers and other related Agencies.
5. Implementation of guidance and supervision towards women and children who are victims as referred to in paragraph (2), paragraph (3) and paragraph (4) shall be conducted through monitoring and evaluation of the targets to be achieved.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Community service is the front line when there is potential for violence against children. Child-Friendly Regency/City (KLA) is a Regency/City that has a Child Rights-based Development system through the Integration of Government Commitment and Resources, Community and Business World that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and Activities to ensure the fulfillment of Child Rights, up to the sub-district and pekon level. 63. Parahita Ekapraya Award (APE) is an award given by the central government to Ministries or Institutions, Provincial and Regency/City Regional Governments for their commitment in efforts to realize gender equality, women's empowerment and child protection. 64. Gender mainstreaming working group hereinafter referred to as Pokja PUG is a consultation forum for implementers and movers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region. 65. Technical Implementation Unit of the Office, hereinafter referred to as UPTD is an organization that carries out operational technical activities and/or certain supporting technical activities at the Office of Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning of Tanggamus Regency. 66. Technical Implementation Unit of the Office of Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Protection hereinafter referred to as UPTD PPA is the Technical Implementation Unit of the Office of Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Protection. 67. Private sector is Non-Governmental Institutions, Business World and Mass Media. 68. Child-Friendly Health Center is a health center that provides services to children completely and integrated while paying attention to children's needs. 69. Child-Friendly School (SRA) is a formal, non-formal, and informal education unit that seeks to guarantee, fulfill, and respect rights, provide protection, and support child participation. 70. Child-friendly Islamic boarding school is an effort to create Islamic boarding schools and their surrounding environment so that children can be comfortable, clean, feel at home, worship devotedly, enjoy learning, playing and interacting. 71. Child-friendly place of worship is a place of worship that provides a comfortable, safe environment, and is appropriate to the needs of children. 72. Women-Friendly and Child-Caring Village (DRPPA) is a village that integrates gender perspective and child rights in the governance of village government administration, village development, as well as community guidance and empowerment, which is carried out in a planned, comprehensive, sustainable manner, in accordance with Indonesia's development vision. 73. Integrated Service and Referral System hereinafter abbreviated as SLRT is a service system that helps identify the needs of the poor and vulnerable based on profiles in the List of Beneficiaries and connects them with social protection and poverty alleviation programs carried out by the central, provincial and regency/city governments according to their needs. 74. Team for Violence against Women and Children or abbreviated as (Tim KtP/A) on Sexual Violence Crimes (TPKS) is the health sector that plays an important role in efforts to fulfill the right to health services for victims of Violence Against Women and Children (KtP/A), especially in recognizing or identifying cases of KtP/A, providing comprehensive services to victims of KtP/A, including making medical, social, and legal referrals.

Article 26

1. The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector and mass media in the protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Partnership with the business sector as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through:

a. Notification of information on employment opportunities for women and children victims of acts of violence;
b. Education and training for women and children victims of acts of violence.

3. Partnership with mass media as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the dissemination of information and educational materials that are beneficial from social, cultural, educational, religious, and health aspects of women and children by taking into account the best interests of women and children victims of violence.

CHAPTER IX

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 28

1. The regional government implements Guidance and Supervision by means of: a. Coordination b. Guidance c. Education and Training d. Monitoring and Evaluation
2. Implementation of coordination as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a shall be conducted among stakeholders in a cross-sectoral manner with Regional Apparatus, and community institutions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
3. Implementation of Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b towards women and children who are victims through guidance on religious values and social values, Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance by the Regional Apparatus in charge together with other related Agencies.
4. Implementation of education and training as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c shall be provided to women and children who are victims as an effort to improve the physical and mental condition of women and children in fulfilling their rights and life needs by the Regional Apparatus in charge, Vocational Training Centers and other related Agencies.
5. Implementation of guidance and supervision towards women and children who are victims as referred to in paragraph (2), paragraph (3) and paragraph (4) shall be conducted through monitoring and evaluation of the targets to be achieved.

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF TANGGAMUS REGENCY

NUMBER 2 YEAR 2024

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN I. GENERAL.

Acts of violence against women and children have experienced an increasingly rising trend. Triggering factors such as economic, social, cultural and social environment are becoming more complex along with the influence of technological development. Concrete steps are needed to provide protection by all elements of Citizens as a unity of society, as well as the role of the Regional Government as protector of its citizens with various programs to prevent acts of violence against women and children. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women and maintain their role and nature as a woman to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their family.

Efforts to prevent violence against children are a shared obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector in a holistic and inseparable manner from one another. Community service is the front line when there is potential for violence against children. The mechanism for preventing violence and protecting child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. Such efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reuniting child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.

In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.
